newsitem.title: CHINA: INTERVIEW - Liu Chong Hing Bank sees China expansion.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Liu Chong Hing Bank sees China expansion.

text.p: Liu Chong Hing Bank Ltd said on Tuesday that it hoped COSCO Pacific Ltd's wide business network in China would allow it to pick up large customers and expand its presence on the mainland.

The medium-sized Hong Kong bank announced earlier that COSCO Pacific, the Hong Kong-listed arm of China's biggest shipping conglomerate China Ocean Shipping (Group) Co, had agreed to take a 20 percent stake in it.
"One of the purposes (of the deal) is that we hope COSCO's suppliers and creditors in China and overseas can give us business," bank director Nam Lee Yick told Reuters.
Nam said in an interview that COSCO Group has departments and representative offices in 26 cities and provinces in China and more than 70 branch offices overseases.
It has a fleet of more than 600 ships calling in more than 1,000 ports in the world, he added.
"We can provide them with trade finance, industrial and commercial finance and other services such as foreign exchange and remittance," said Nam.
He said COSCO could also boost Liu Chong Hing Bank's presence in China where its current operations are mainly in Southern China and focused on small customers.
"Since our China business now relies on Hong Kong's small trade and commercial accounts, and we don't have big customers in China, we hope to get big customers through the deal," he said.
Liu Chong Hing Bank has a representative office in Shanghai and a branch in Shantou.
Under current Chinese regulations, Nam said Liu Chong Hing Bank would not be able to open more branches in China in the short term since its assets fell short of required levels.
Liu Chong Hing currently has assets totalling HK$32 billion (US$4.13 billion).
"Eventually we will open more branches in China, maybe in several years since we probably have to wait until China amends this rule," said Nam.
Liu Chong Hing Bank has 33 branches in Hong Kong and plans to open two more by the end of the year.

It said earlier on Tuesday it would raise HK$1.07 billion (US$138 million) for general funding purposes through the issue of 45 million new shares to Liu Chong Hing Estate Ltd, a wholly-owned unit of controlling shareholder Liu Chong Hing Investment Ltd.
COSCO Pacific Ltd in turn agreed to buy 64 million shares in Liu Chong Hing Bank from Liu Chong Hing Estate and five million shares from the Liu family for a total HK$1.65 billion.
It also said it would buy a further 20 million Liu Chong Hing Bank shares, or a five percent stake, from its parent COSCO (Hong Kong) Group Ltd for HK$477.60 million.
After the transactions, Liu Chong Hing Estate would have a 43.98 percent stake in Liu Chong Hing Bank compared with the current 53.68 percent.
COSCO Pacific would have a 20 percent stake and the Liu family would hold 3.97 percent compared with the current 5.66 percent.
